#Text=But come in and eat supper with us,
#Text=for we have many things to talk about.

_	_	_	

#Text=I accept the invitation with more pleasure than you are aware of,

column1: #Text=because the exquisite flavor of the pickled salmon that I ate for
#Text=breakfast is still lingering in my mouth, and I long for another taste."
#Text=We humored our friend by complying with his hint, and after we had
#Text=finished our tea, we lighted our pipes, talked business, and broached a
#Text=subject to Smith, which we had entertained ever since we had decided to
#Text=go into business.
#Text=There was no response for a moment, and then the slow, cautious movement
#Text=began again.
#Text="Strike a light," whispered Fred, "and let us see what this means."
#Text=Among the effects which we had found in the store was a large lamp for
#Text=burning alcohol; this Fred had cleansed and trimmed the day before, and
#Text=filled with spirits of turpentine, for the purpose of using it in
#Text=cooking.
#Text=I knew where it was placed; so I crept carefully along on my
#Text=hands and knees, and suddenly lighted it with a lucifer.
#Text=As the huge
#Text=wick took fire, I hastily glanced over my shoulder, for fear that an
#Text=assassin should strike a blow before I could be on my guard.
#Text=A startling yell from Fred caused me to spring to my feet, and as I did
#Text=so, a long, dark object flashed before my eyes, and narrowly missed my
#Text=head.
#Text=The next instant my yell of terror was added to Fred  '  s, for in the
#Text=middle of the floor, with waving tail, and eyes that blazed like coals
#Text=of fire, was a monstrous snake of a jet black hue; the huge mouth of the
#Text=reptile was thrown open to its widest extent, and was armed with fangs
#Text=This circumstance required our movements to be prompt if we wished to
#Text=surprise the ruffians, but Mr.
#Text=Wright was not a man to be hurried by
#Text=such trifles.
#Text=He had a peculiar idea of how such matters should be
#Text=conducted, and neither Mr.
#Text=Brown nor myself were disposed to interfere
#Text=with his plans.
#Text=Suddenly, when within twenty rods of the place where the bushrangers
#Text=were camped we saw a light, and for a few minutes Mr.
#Text=Wright was
#Text=uncertain whether to advance or retreat, thinking that the light was
#Text=intended as an ambush to draw us under fire.
#Text=In vain I explained that the bushrangers had kindled a fire for the
#Text=purpose of cooking a sheep, or a portion of one, and Mr.
#Text=Brown
#Text=entertained the same idea, but Mr.
#Text=Wright said we were young men, and
#Text=rash at that, and that we were not to be trusted.
#Text=We were more amazed than indignant, knowing that our host regarded our
#Text=safety more than his own, for he was as brave as a lion, and would have
#Text=willingly fought the whole gang had it been necessary to prove his
#Text=courage.
#Text=At length I volunteered to act the part of a scout, and investigate
#Text=matters, but for a long time Mr.
#Text=Wright would not listen to my advances,
#Text=until I saw that there was a prospect of our remaining on the ground all
#Text=night, and then I tore myself away, and requested my friends to remain
#Text=quiet until my return.
#Text=This they promised to do, and I started on my mission, not a dangerous
#Text=one, as I knew full well, for the ruffians did not suspect the presence
#Text=of our force, and I felt certain that they had no sentinels posted.
#Text=The result justified my expectations, for when I had crawled as
#Text=noiselessly as a cat to within a rod of the light, I saw that the
#Text=robbers had in some way managed to kindle a fire, which, by the way,
#Text=attracted myriads of flies and mosquitoes, and they were biting as only
#Text=Australian flies and mosquitoes know how to bite, much to the rage of
#Text=the bushrangers, who were cooking meat, and endeavoring to beat off the
#Text=cloud of insects by threshing their heavy hands about their heads, and
#Text=uttering oaths that were frightfully original and emphatic.
#Text=They were coarse-looking fellows, but dressed better than bushrangers
#Text=usually were, and I accounted for it by supposing that they had made a
#Text=successful plundering expedition, and got new suits from their victims;
#Text=and such I afterwards found to be the case.
#Text=I endeavored to get a view of the faces of the women, and by changing my
#Text=position I succeeded.
#Text=The youngest one was not more than twenty-five
#Text=years of age, but she looked careworn and weary, and seldom removed her
#Text=hands from her face, except, to answer a question addressed to her by
#Text=her companion, who seemed about forty years of age, and by the
#Text=flickering light of the fire I read determination upon every line of her
#Text=countenance, weather-beaten and grim as it was.
#Text=The bushrangers were broiling their meat upon sticks, and eating it with
#Text=a relish that smacked of a long fast; and while the women were seated
#Text=near the fire on saddles taken from the horses, which were tied to a
#Text=tree, and were browsing upon the tender branches, the men did not offer
#Text=them food, until one fellow, whose appetite seemed sated, offered the
#Text=younger one his stick, upon which was a huge lump of flesh nearly raw.
#Text=She declined the tempting morsel with a shudder, and the action produced
#Text=an oath from the ruffian, and an insulting gesture, so vile that I could
#Text=hardly keep my hand from seeking the lock of my revolver and shooting
#Text=him on the spot.
